created_at_note: timestamps written at first ledger append; this file hashed BEFORE any held-out evaluation ran
question: Do archived elites behave as transferable skills on unseen mazes / shifted starts, or are they maze-memorization?

platform.evaluation_mode: batched (validate.py batching, 256) used for ALL conditions identically; source-maze baseline re-measured on this platform, stored archive fitness NOT used as baseline
platform.platform_warning: full-archive batch replay on this platform diverges from stored values for some elites (chaotic collision dynamics amplify FP differences); single-elite replay matches exactly. All comparisons in THIS study are internal to this platform and mode.

material.elites_per_archive: all retained elites, archive order fixed across all conditions

held_out_mazes.generator: same grammar as source maze: 2 horizontal walls (lower y~U(0.26,0.38), upper y~U(0.58,0.70), thickness 0.035, gap on opposite sides, gap width 0.28), optional top-room blade, 4 pillars r~U(0.06,0.09); all rng from np.random.default_rng(maze_seed)
validity_rules_applied_in_order_determin: START (0.06,0.06) and 4 shifted starts (±0.02 in x/y) free
free-area ratio within [0.75, 1.15] x source-maze free-area ratio
flood-fill reachable free grid-centers (64x64, from START) >= 0.55 of free centers
first 6 pool seeds passing all rules are taken; rejected candidates logged with rule violated, none skipped silently

baselines.random_per_maze: n=256 fresh genomes, N(0,1.2) clipped +/-4, rng=np.random.default_rng(1000000+maze_seed), identical for every archive/condition on that maze

secondary: cell_transfer_fraction (same 64x64 cell as source-maze endpoint; descriptive)

hypotheses.claim: Elites retain meaningful quality on unseen mazes (transferable skill, not pure memorization).
hypotheses.test_plan: All retained elites of each primary archive evaluated on 6 held-out mazes vs same-maze fresh-random baseline n=256; mean over mazes, all 3 archives reported, none dropped.
hypotheses.verdict_rule: SUPPORTED_IN_THIS_LAB if both thresholds met on the mean; REJECTED_BY_THRESHOLD if mean retention < 0.75 OR mean advantage < 0.15; UNKNOWN otherwise (e.g. high variance across archives)
hypotheses.kill_condition: If elite mean fitness on held-out mazes <= random baseline + 0.05, the archive is labeled maze-memorization; no threshold may be changed after observing results.

hypotheses.claim: On the SAME maze, elites tolerate small start perturbations (robustness of skill, not of trajectory memory).
hypotheses.test_plan: Source maze, starts shifted by 0.02 in each cardinal direction; all primary archives; retention vs SOURCE start.
hypotheses.verdict_rule: SUPPORTED_IN_THIS_LAB if both met; REJECTED_BY_THRESHOLD if mean < 0.90 or any single retention < 0.80; UNKNOWN otherwise
hypotheses.kill_condition: If retention collapses (<0.5) on any single 0.02 shift, skill is start-locked; record as negative finding.

inference_limits: toy 2D point-robot maze; no real robot, no market, no OCTOPUS Core involvement
3 evolved archives from 1 environment grammar; generalization claim bounded to this grammar
no p-values; descriptive means over seeds/mazes; negative results preserved verbatim
